startup.name: Expanse
startup.one_liner: Twice the work from the GPUs you already own
startup.description: Software that predicts the compute each AI workload needs before it runs, so organisations get more work from their existing GPU clusters, on their own hardware. Four engineers from quantitative hedge fund GPU operations, based in London.

yc_acceptance.basis: Placeholder value only, because Expanse is already known to be accepted. Test note: accepted to YC, so the acceptance step is not forecast. The prior is about 1 percent. Four technical founders with direct operating experience of the problem would sit above the prior (founder market fit is the top success tag in the repo data).
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most plausibly pass because GPU scheduling is crowded by Run:ai, Slurm tooling and cloud vendors, and prediction accuracy claims are hard to verify. A London team without customers could also appear too early for a sales-led infrastructure product. The interview would test whether the founders can show proof of demand, speed of shipping and a reason the market is open now for Expanse.

outcomes.why_it_fails: Likely stall or small acquisition. GPU tooling analogs (Trainy, Thunder Compute, Luminal) are early and most stay small, and the category's leader Run:ai was absorbed by a hardware vendor. A large outcome requires becoming the standard planning layer for enterprise AI compute, which cloud and hardware vendors have strong incentive to own.

killers.risk: Seen as a feature of Slurm, Kubernetes and Run:ai style schedulers
killers.evidence: Run:ai is a Kubernetes native scheduler that optimizes GPU utilization and existing cluster tooling already collects telemetry.
killers.mitigation: Integrate with existing schedulers rather than replacing them.

killers.risk: Prediction accuracy does not hold across diverse workloads
killers.evidence: A 2026 study found Slurm metadata alone is largely non-informative for runtime behavior and needs live telemetry.
killers.mitigation: Use telemetry and publish measured utilization gains.

killers.risk: Small buyer pool and long sales cycles
killers.evidence: Organisations with large owned GPU fleets are few, and Trainy has not shown a round despite logos.
killers.mitigation: Land hedge funds and labs where founders have relationships.

killers.evidence: Nvidia owns Run:ai and DCGM telemetry and has the distribution.
killers.mitigation: Stay vendor neutral across Nvidia and AMD.

technical_complexity.rationale: Accurate prediction of GPU memory and runtime before execution needs profiling, modeling and integration with schedulers. The founders' experience helps, but robust coverage across frameworks is hard for four people.

takeover_risk.rationale: Nvidia and schedulers have telemetry, customers and incentive to add prediction. A rival could ship basic features in about a year.

evidence.claim: Enterprises measure idle GPUs and use telemetry to reduce idleness, showing a paid pain.
Research shows GPU over-allocation wastes cluster capacity and prediction can raise utilization.

roadmap.goal: Show prediction accuracy on real workloads.
actions: Benchmark prediction on public cluster traces
Run a free pilot on one fund or lab cluster
roadmap.proof: Prediction error under 10% on a real workload set

actions: Convert two pilots to annual licenses
roadmap.proof: $250K or more of contracted annual revenue

pros.point: Founders ran the clusters they are optimizing
pros.evidence: The team is described as engineers who managed GPU clusters at large quant funds.

pros.point: Measurable value on scarce, expensive hardware
pros.evidence: GPU idleness and over-allocation are quantified in industry and academic reports.

brand.rationale: A short real word that fits compute but is shared with other products, so search and trademark clarity is weaker. Infrastructure buyers care little about names, so it moves no probability.

narrative.headline: Strong founder market fit in a crowded scheduler space, with a seed likely and a Series A a coin flip below even odds.
narrative.general_summary: Expanse predicts the compute each AI workload needs so organisations can use existing GPU clusters more efficiently. The founders operated such clusters at large quantitative funds, which is a strong signal. GPU scarcity gives the pain real dollar value. The risks are that Nvidia, Run:ai and schedulers bundle the capability, buyers are few, and sales cycles are long. YC analogs in GPU tooling such as Trainy and Luminal raised small seeds or none, and Thunder Compute reached a Series A with a distinct product. A seed within a year is likely, a Series A requires paid enterprise deployments.
